chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about a man who has sexual intercourse with a woman, is she permissible for his son? Or if the son has sexual intercourse with her, is she permissible for his father? He said: If the father or the son touched her and took from her (consummated), then she is not permissible.

key_terms.يَفْجُرُ: to have sexual intercourse (specifically in marriage or concubinage context)

ai.seo_question: Does a father and son both marrying the same woman make her haram to both of them in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the specific condition for the prohibition of 'illat al-furuj' (impediment due to sexual intercourse), ruling that the woman becomes prohibited to both father and son only if both have actually consummated the relationship with her. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining whether the impediment is permanent or if the prohibition applies solely to the specific pair who engaged in intercourse, reflecting the juristic debate on whether the act itself or the possession of the woman is the primary cause of prohibition.
